{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''José Nathan Kutz''' is the Robert Bolles and Yasuko Endo Professor within the Department of Applied Mathematics at the [[University of Washington]] in Seattle. His main research interests involve non-linear waves and coherent structures (especially in [[fiber laser]]s), as well as [[dimensionality reduction]] and data-analysis techniques for complex systems.<ref name="cv">[http://faculty.washington.edu/kutz/cv.html Curriculum vitae], retrieved 2015-04-27.</ref>

He graduated from the University of Washington with a B.S. in 1990,<ref name="cv"/> and obtained his PhD in 1994 at [[Northwestern University]], supervised by William L. Kath.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=79827}}</ref>

He is the author of the book ''Data-Driven Modeling & Scientific Computation: Methods for Complex Systems & Big Data'' (Oxford Univ. Press, 2013). He also delivers on a regular basis ''Scientific Computing'' and ''Computational Methods for Data Analysis'' as Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) in the [[Coursera]] platform.

He was elected as a Fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], in the 2022 Class of [[SIAM Fellow]]s, "for contributions to applied dynamical systems, machine learning, and nonlinear optics".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-announces-class-of-2022-fellows|title=SIAM Announces Class of 2022 Fellows|date=March 31, 2022|work=SIAM News|access-date=2022-03-31|archive-date=2022-04-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220413000118/https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-announces-class-of-2022-fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref>
